Earthy, dry and nothing like the vegetable.

How to use

  • Add 2 drops to a 30 ml bottle of rosehip for a night oil.
  • Dilute to 1% — the smell is strong and earthy.
  • Blend with frankincense and geranium for a facial blend.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Dry earth
  • Hay
  • Faint root

What's in it

  • 100% pure Daucus carota seed oil

Who it's for

Mature or dry skin

A long-standing component of facial oil blends, usually at 1% or less.

People who like earthy scents

Dry and rooty, with nothing sweet about it.

Blenders who want an unusual base

Distinctive enough that one drop changes the character of a blend entirely.

What people get wrong

Expecting it to smell of carrots. It is distilled from the seed of wild carrot, not the root, and smells of dry earth and hay instead.

Using too much. The smell is strong and earthy, and at more than a drop or two it dominates everything else in a facial oil.

What it won't do

Carrot seed essential oil and carrot-infused carrier oil are different products sold under similar names. This is the distilled essential oil, used by the drop.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Carrot Seed

Is this the same as carrot oil for skin?

No. Carrot-infused oil is a carrier, usually sunflower or coconut, with carrot root steeped in it — used by the spoonful. This is the distilled essential oil from the seeds, used by the drop.

Why does it smell earthy rather than sweet?

Because it comes from the seed of wild carrot rather than the cultivated root. None of the sugars that make a carrot sweet are volatile, so none of them carry across in distillation.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. Avoid during pregnancy. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.
